newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Reliance starts new PTA unit.
newsitem.headline: India's Reliance starts new PTA unit.

text.p: Petrochemicals firm Reliance Industries Ltd on Friday said it commissioned its 350,000 tonnes per annum (tpa) PTA (purified terephthalic acid) plant at its Hazira petrochemical works on the west coast.
A company spokesman said the new plant has achieved 100 percent of rated capacity in less than a week's time. PTA is the major raw material for polyester.
"With the commissioning of the new plant, Reliance's total annual PTA capacity will exceed 600,000 tonnes," it said.
Reliance's existing PTA plant at Patalganga in western India was built in 1987 and has a current capacity of 250,000 tonnes per year, Reliance said in a statement.
A third PTA plant of 350,000 tpa is currently under construction, also at Hazira, and is in an advanced stage of implementation, the company said.
"On completion of this project, Reliance's total PTA production capacity will exceed one million tonnes, making it the fifth largest producer of PTA in the world," it said.
Reliance is currently the only Indian producer of this chemical, the preferred raw material for making polyester.

The supply and demand for polyester in India have increased at an annual compounded rate of 20 percent and 19 percent respectively over the past 10 years, leading to a high growth rate for PTA, Reliance said.

The consumption of PTA and its substitute DMT is expected to be around one million tonnes in 1997/98 (April-March), showing a compounded annual growth rate of about 20 percent over the past 10 years, the company said.
It said the global PTA/DMT demand industry has grown at the rate of 9.0 percent during the same period, it said.
